subject: Request: one-off usage adjustment & amendment to committed capacity
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: AvaCloud Billing <billing@avacloud.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice — request for review

Hi Rishi,

We just received our November invoice and it includes a one-time charge of $9,400 listed as a post-term usage true-up. This seems to be for a burst in API tokens the week after we renewed, which we believe was tied to an internal experiment that should have been covered by the renewal windows.

Can you help us understand the breakdown and whether there's flexibility on this one-off? If we have to pay, we'd like to understand options for smoothing this into next term or applying a credit while we increase our committed capacity.

I've attached the usage export from our side for Nov 15–22 (usage_report_nov2026.csv) for your reference.

Thanks,
Emma Zhao
Head of ML Platforms
AvaCloud

(Attachment: usage_report_nov2026.csv)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice — request for review

Hi Emma — thanks for flagging and for the CSV. Appreciate the quick heads-up.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I'll pull the server-side invoice breakout and confirm what portion is post-term activity vs. pro-rated renewal timing.
- Looping in Lauren (billing) to propose an adjustment or credit, and Ben (revenue ops) to weigh in on precedent/approval.
- If helpful, we can offer a short-term amendment to increase committed capacity so this doesn't recur and to offset the one-off.

Lauren/Ben — attaching AvaCloud's usage export. Priority ask: can we either (A) waive the one-off entirely as a one-time courtesy, (B) issue a partial credit and propose a capacity upsell amendment, or (C) bill as-is but provide a repayment/amortization plan? Emma is suggesting they will sign an amendment if we can meet them halfway.

Thanks — I can be available for a quick call today if needed.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

> On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io> wrote:
> > [original message and attachment omitted]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>; Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T15:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice — request for review

Hi Emma and Rishi — I pulled the ledger and matched token-level usage across the spike window. A few notes: 
- The $9,400 is entirely post-renewal usage outside the committed cap. The granular export lines up with your CSV.
- Historically we've seen two common approaches: credit a percentage as a customer goodwill one-off, or apply a one-time bill but immediately convert an equivalent dollar amount into committed capacity for the next 12 months (effectively prepaying).

Proposal (for internal approval):
- Offer a 60% goodwill credit on the one-off ($5,640) contingent on AvaCloud signing a 12-month committed capacity amendment for +30% baseline throughput (DocuSign link to follow).
- We would apply the credit to the current invoice and create the amendment starting next billing period.

I've attached a draft of the amendment/proforma (proposed_amendment_draft.pdf) and the usage reconciliation CSV for transparency. If you prefer a different split (e.g., 50/50 credit + amortization) say so and we'll model it.

Emma — if an exec wants to weigh in, we can also escalate to revenue leadership but this should be within our delegation with Ben's signoff.

Lauren Bishop
Billing Manager
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: proposed_amendment_draft.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice — request for review

Thanks Lauren — that approach sounds reasonable. A few clarifying points before I sign off: 
1) Confirm the committed uplift (30%) translates to a $7,500 increase in ARR for AvaCloud on an annualized basis. We need that math in the DocuSign amendment.
2) For one-off credit, I'd be comfortable with 50–70% credit range; 60% is fine if we lock a 12-month term and receive signed amendment within 10 business days.
3) If AvaCloud prefers amortization instead of an immediate amendment, offer a 6-month amortization on remaining balance with automatic renewal of a baseline commit at current levels.

I'll prepare an approval note and route to finance. Rishi — can you nudge Emma to confirm which option she prefers (credit+amendment vs amortization)? Also confirm billing contact for updated invoice.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

> On Nov 22, 2026, at 3:27 PM, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > [proposal and attachments omitted]

From: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@avacloud.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice — request for review

Hi all — thanks for the quick turn. AvaCloud is willing to accept the 60% one-time credit contingent on the 12-month +30% committed capacity amendment. We'll route to procurement and should have the signed DocuSign within the 10 business days you mentioned.

Please:
- Apply the $5,640 credit to the current invoice so we don't get a past-due notice.
- Send the updated invoice and the DocuSign link to procurement@avacloud.io.

We'll sign and return the amendment; appreciate you working with us on this.

Best,
Emma Zhao
Head of ML Platforms, AvaCloud
